notes: Clean Qwen3-235B NeMo-RL Full-GRPO result; non-colocated generation avoids the colocated TP4 host-memory OOM and preserves generation TP4. Shutdown emitted recvBytes noise after all timing metrics.

First Qwen3-235B decode-heavy ramp beyond fixed256; NeMo-RL latest-main worker venv with vLLM 0.20.0, fixed decode 1024, max_model_len 8192, max_num_batched_tokens 16384. PARD K3 remains strongly positive in steady-state Step2-3.

Aggressive K9 fixed256 gate on the same clean non-colocated TP4 shape. It is faster than the matched baseline, but acceptance is much lower than K3/K5 OpenMath expectations. High-batch standalone batch64/128 favors K5 over K9, so K9 should not be the static high-batch default without an adaptive controller.

Matched K5 fixed256 gate on the same clean non-colocated TP4 shape after high-batch standalone batch64/128 favored K5 over K9. It is slightly slower than K9 but acceptance is much better, so K5 is the preferred static high-batch candidate. A 20-step K5 stability run was submitted as 3211900.

Matched GBS512 performance gate requested after GBS256 was reclassified as functional/stability only. Earlier K5 attempts 3212013 and 3212068 failed before valid metrics due checkpoint-path readiness and Ray head/GCS startup respectively, not OOM. Retry2 3212209 completed 5/5 with no fatal/OOM pattern and confirms K5 remains strongly positive at GBS512.

Matched GBS512 static K3 gate submitted after OpenMath high-batch standalone favored K3. It completed 5/5 with no OOM and remains strongly faster than baseline, but it is slower than static K5 3212209: K5 is about 1.133x faster in total step and 1.182x faster in generation time. K5 remains the NeMo-RL GBS512 static baseline.

Dynamic-K medium16 GBS512 run after the actor venv marker smoke 3213497. Runtime logs showed selected=3 tier=large for dense requests=32 and selected=5 only on small tail batches. It completed 5/5 without OOM and is positive vs baseline, but it is slower than static K5 3212209 and nearly identical to static K3 3212919. K5 remains the validated NeMo-RL GBS512 default; medium16 dynamic-K is useful as runtime proof, not as the best current policy.
GBS2048 official recipe shape with mem80 and max_num_batched_tokens 16384; PARD gives clear generation speedup but E2E gain is limited because generation is only 21.7% of baseline step time.
Small-model stability gate; target generation TP2 and draft TP2. This is a fixed256 conservative vLLM memory envelope, not the original 4096-token performance YAML.
Small-model GBS2048 stability gate completed 20/20 with no Step-3 CuMem OOM. Target generation TP2 and draft TP2; fixed256 mem80/bt16k envelope.

Negative control for the runtime request gate. Shape matches the valid GBS512 K5 performance pair, but VLLM_SPECDEC_BATCH_SIZE_GATE_THRESHOLD=16 disables speculation in the dense max_num_seqs=32 phase. No acceptance buckets emitted. Result is baseline-like, not a SpecDec win: static K5 job 3212209 remains 1.779x faster in total step and 2.293x faster in generation than this gate16 run. Use this to justify true dynamic-K/controller work rather than static on/off gating.
